transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I came in today because... well, my eating just went completely off the rails recently. I'm usually pretty strict about my food tracking, but I just stopped caring about it entirely. I was skipping real meals for days on end, pretty much just living on coffee and protein bars. Honestly, I didn't even realize how bad it got until my clothes started hanging loose on me.
Were you avoiding food because you were afraid of gaining weight or becoming larger?

No, it wasn't about weight at all. I wasn't looking in the mirror thinking I was too big or anything like that. I just... I didn't feel the need to eat. It was more like food was a waste of time, or I was just too wired to even think about sitting down for a meal. I just didn't care about it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight because of this change in eating?

Yeah, I have. Like I mentioned with my clothes starting to hang loose on me, it was pretty noticeable once I actually paid attention to it. I haven't stepped on a scale to give you an exact number of pounds, but it's definitely a significant amount of weight to lose just from skipping meals for days at a time.
Are you avoiding eating because you fear something unpleasant might happen, such as choking, vomiting, or becoming ill?

No, it's nothing like that. I'm not scared of choking or throwing up or anything. Like I said, I just didn't feel the need to eat. It wasn't about being afraid of the food or what it would do to me. I just didn't care to stop what I was doing to eat it.
During the period when you were eating very little, did you have an unusually elevated or irritable mood?

Yeah, I did. I felt... I don't know, almost unstoppable for days. Like my mind was just brilliant, moving a million miles a minute. But at the same time, if someone interrupted me or asked me a basic question, or even just slowed me down, I'd get really irritable. I would snap at them, like they were deliberately trying to sabotage the whole company or ruin what I was working on. So, yeah, it was this mix of feeling amazing but also getting really angry if anyone got in my way.
How long did that unusually elevated or irritable mood last?

I'd say... well, this whole episode built over about three weeks. It really started right after I was handed some temporary PMO-level responsibility at work. So, yeah, it was going on for about three weeks.
How much did this period interfere with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

It interfered a lot. Work basically fell apart. I was... well, I missed important handoffs, and I kept sending out these strategy documents that apparently no one could follow. It got to the point where my manager and corporate security actually ended up taking me to the emergency department. 

And at home, it wasn't any better. I just stopped keeping up with normal meals, my hobbies... just basic routines completely went out the window.
During this period, did you need much less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?

Yeah, definitely. I was... I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, tops. And I would wake up feeling completely charged. It honestly felt like sleep was just this inefficient process that I had somehow managed to optimize right out of my schedule. I didn't feel tired at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a three-week episode of abnormally elevated and irritable mood with markedly reduced need for sleep, racing thoughts, increased activation, reduced eating with significant weight loss, and severe occupational and functional impairment requiring emergency evaluation. No psychotic symptoms were reported. The presentation is most consistent with a manic episode without psychotic symptoms in bipolar affective disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Markedly irritable mood when interrupted or slowed down
Racing thoughts and feeling that the mind was moving very rapidly
Markedly reduced need for sleep, sleeping approximately two to three hours nightly while feeling fully rested
Increased activation and preoccupation with work projects
Reduced eating and significant unintentional weight loss during the episode
Severe impairment in occupational functioning, including missed handoffs and incomprehensible strategy documents
Severe disruption of daily routines and self-care

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Abnormally elevated and irritable mood and associated symptoms persisted for approximately three weeks.
additional_requirements: Marked occupational and daily-life impairment was explicitly confirmed.
Emergency department evaluation was required because of the severity of the episode.
No fear of weight gain, body-image disturbance, choking, vomiting, or illness related to eating was reported.
